summary.text: Jeff Turco is a Democratic state representative from the 19th Suffolk District who has served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives since April 2021 and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
An attorney with a private practice in Chelsea, he previously served as Winthrop Town Council president and as special sheriff of Worcester County.

paragraphs.text: Jeff Turco is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he earned a B.A. in history, and of Quinnipiac University Law School; he also studied law at Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland.
His official biography says he is licensed to practice law in Massachusetts and Connecticut and has his own private practice in Chelsea.
Turco served six years as chief of staff to former State Senator Guy Glodis and five years as Special Sheriff and Superintendent of the Worcester County Sheriff's Office.
He was Winthrop's Town Council president in 2010 and 2011 and later chaired the town's Charter Review Commission, and he served multiple terms on the Democratic State Committee.
Turco was first elected in a March 2021 special election and was sworn in on April 7, 2021.
His district includes all of Winthrop and about 45 percent of Revere.

He is vice chair of the Joint Committee on Veterans and Federal Affairs and also serves on the House Committee on Federal Funding, Policy and Accountability and the Joint Committees on Emergency Preparedness and Management and on Telecommunications, Utilities and Energy.
Turco is married to Melissa Turco, and they have six children.
